summary: Kaletha introduces rigid inner forms of real and p-adic groups: a Galois gerbe u → W bound by a profinite multiplicative group, the cohomology H^1(u → W, Z → G), and a Tate–Nakayama-type isomorphism (Theorems 4.8 and 4.11). He uses them to normalize transfer factors across inner forms and to state the refined local Langlands correspondence, proved here for tempered real groups. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and fifteen findings are recorded. E01–E06 follow the author's errata. Corollary 5.4 (E05) and the §3.4 isomorphism criterion (E07) are false as printed; after review E08 and E10–E13 affect nothing. Not formalised.

items.name: Absolute Galois group
items.statement: For a field F, Gamma is Aut_F(Fsep) with its Krull topology; it is topologically isomorphic to the algebraic-closure version.
items.note: Only the stated pinned carrier or theorem is credited. Additional specialized API and tests are planning contracts, not certified implementations.

api.name: Kaletha16.L20.construct

items.name: Discrete units and Kummer coefficients
items.statement: For any field F and natural n, the additive versions of Fsep units and its n-th roots of unity carry their actual continuous Gamma actions and the discrete topology.

items.statement: For a topological additive coefficient group with continuous action, the low-degree continuous cocycle/coboundary quotients H1 and H2 exist under the pinned continuity hypotheses. items.name: Finite-extension Hilbert 90
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional field extension L/F, every multiplicative one-cocycle Aut_F(L) -> L units is a coboundary, so the abstract group H1 is trivial.
items.note: Only the stated pinned carrier or theorem is credited. Additional specialized API and tests are planning contracts, not certified implementations.

items.name: Tate degree-zero norm quotient
items.statement: For a finite group acting on a module over a commutative ring, Tate H0 is invariants modulo the image of the norm.

items.name: Tate degree-minus-one norm kernel
items.statement: For a finite group acting on a module over a commutative ring, Tate H(-1) is the norm kernel modulo the augmentation submodule.
items.note: Only the stated pinned carrier or theorem is credited. Additional specialized API and tests are planning contracts, not certified implementations.

items.name: Abstract extension classification by H2
items.statement: For an abstract group Gamma acting on an abelian group M, normalized factor sets modulo coboundaries correspond to H2; extensions inducing that action are equivalent exactly when their section factor sets have the same class. No topology or continuous section is part of this credit.
items.note: Only the stated pinned carrier or theorem is credited. Additional specialized API and tests are planning contracts, not certified implementations.

items.name: Continuous Hilbert 90 and Kummer comparison
items.statement: For a field F, continuous H1(Gamma,Fsep units) vanishes; for n invertible in F the connecting map identifies F units/(F units)^n with H1(Gamma,mu_n), retaining its cyclotomic action.

items.name: Finite quotient and Shapiro comparisons
items.statement: For profinite Gamma and discrete continuous abelian coefficients, continuous cohomology is the compatible finite-quotient colimit; induction/coinduction from an open subgroup gives the Shapiro isomorphisms with restriction/corestriction compatibility.

items.name: Compact-coefficient derived inverse-limit comparison
items.statement: For a profinite group G and a countable tower A_n of finite discrete continuous abelian G-modules, A=lim A_n with its actual inverse-limit topology satisfies, for q≥1, 0→lim¹H^(q−1)(G,A_n)→H^q_cts(G,A)→lim H^q(G,A_n)→0; H0 commutes with the limit. Surjective transitions are not required. Mittag–Leffler of H^(q−1), in particular its levelwise finiteness, kills the obstruction. Degree one is unconditional because invariants of finite coefficients are finite. Degree two needs the H1 hypothesis, supplied for the local fields here by P23.

items.name: Continuous Hochschild–Serre and transgression
items.statement: For a profinite extension and the continuous abelian coefficients used here, construct inflation, restriction, the Hochschild–Serre edge sequence and its transgression, with explicit cochain sign convention.

items.name: Local finite-module duality
items.statement: For F a finite extension of Qp and finite discrete Gamma-module M, Tate local duality pairs H^i(F,M) perfectly with H^(2-i)(F,M dual(1)) using inv_F:H2(F,Fsep units)->Q/Z, including p-primary coefficients.

items.name: Real Tate duality
items.statement: For F=R and finite Galois coefficients, use modified Tate cohomology for Gamma=C2 and the real Brauer invariant to obtain the finite dualities used to compute H2(R,u).

items.name: Local class formations and relative Weil extensions
items.statement: For finite Galois E/F of nonarchimedean characteristic-zero local fields, construct its fundamental class and relative Weil extension, normalized invariant 1/[E:F], quotient maps for towers, and transfer/norm compatibility.

items.name: Norm subgroups and local existence
items.statement: The norm subgroups N_(E/F) E units of finite abelian extensions form the local reciprocity neighborhoods required in the vanishing argument for the projective system u.

items.name: Weil restriction and finite central quotients
items.statement: For finite separable E/F and positive n, form Res_(E/F)mu_n and its diagonal mu_n quotient as affine multiplicative-type groups. Over E their characters identify with the permutation module and its augmentation kernel.

api.name: Kaletha16.P09.construct
api.statement: Construct restriction of scalars and the diagonal central quotient.

api.name: Kaletha16.P09.characterise
api.statement: Identify the quotient character module with augmentation-zero elements of (Z/n)[Gal(E/F)] when E/F is Galois.

api.name: Kaletha16.P09.transport
api.statement: Transport the group and character maps along field towers and divisibility of n.

uses.how: Finite-level algebraic carrier for u.

items.name: Local finiteness of ordinary nonabelian H1
items.statement: For a linear algebraic group H over R or a finite extension of Qp, H1(Gamma,H(Fbar)) is finite; this applies to every cocycle-twisted affine group occurring in the fibers below.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

items.name: Fundamental tori and cohomology surjectivity
items.statement: For a connected reductive local group G, a fundamental maximal torus S gives the ordinary H1 surjectivity used in§3.3 and§4.7; for p-adic Gsc every inner twist has trivial H1. Preserve the real anisotropic/fundamental hypotheses.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

items.name: Ordinary Tate–Nakayama for tori
items.statement: For a local torus S split by finite Galois E/F, the fundamental class gives a natural isomorphism (X_*(S)_Gamma)_tors -> H1(F,S), and pairings for the two-term torus complexes used in relative transfer are compatible with norm, restriction and central isogenies.

items.name: Ordinary inner twists and abelianized H1
items.statement: For connected reductive G/F, an inner twist psi:G_Fbar->Gprime_Fbar has psi^-1 sigma(psi) inner; ordinary abelianized H1 is the crossed-module cohomology of Gsc->G, with its map from H1(G).

api.name: Kaletha16.P13.construct
api.statement: Construct the adjoint cocycle of an inner twist.

api.name: Kaletha16.P13.characterise
api.statement: Express abelianization through the crossed module Gsc->G.

api.name: Kaletha16.P13.transport
api.statement: Transport the class by an isomorphism of inner twists.

uses.how: The rigid construction enlarges this already owned ordinary theory.

items.name: Dual groups and central isogenies
items.statement: For connected reductive G and finite central Z, form Gbar=G/Z and the dual isogeny Gbar_hat->G_hat with its based root-data Galois action, compatible maximal tori and coroot lattices.

api.name: Kaletha16.P14.construct
api.statement: Dualize the finite central quotient.

api.name: Kaletha16.P14.characterise
api.statement: Identify the kernel through the character/cocharacter lattice inclusion.

api.name: Kaletha16.P14.transport
api.statement: Transport Levi inclusions and Galois actions through the dual root datum.

uses.how: Carrier for the plus preimages and refined endoscopy.

items.name: Weyl action on cocharacters modulo coroots
items.statement: For maximal tori S1,S2 of connected reductive G, conjugation identifies X_*(Si)/Qvee independently of the conjugating element and equivariantly for Gamma; homomorphisms of reductive groups induce compatible maps.

items.name: Real representation foundation
items.statement: For real reductive groups, construct admissible (g,K)-modules, infinitesimal equivalence and the smooth moderate-growth globalization framework needed for real tempered representations. The analytic character theorem is the separate P18 contract.

items.name: Smooth p-adic representation foundation
items.statement: For reductive p-adic groups with complex coefficients, use smooth admissible irreducible representations, normalized parabolic induction and temperedness in the stated matrix-coefficient sense.

items.name: Projective multiplicative group u
items.statement: For F=R or finite over Qp, index finite Galois E/F and positive n by field extension and divisibility. Set u_(E/F,n)=Res_(E/F)mu_n/mu_n and u=lim u_(E/F,n); u(Fbar) has its profinite topology.

api.name: Kaletha16.D01.construct
api.statement: Construct the directed system and its inverse limit as a pro-multiplicative group.

api.name: Kaletha16.D01.characterise
api.statement: Its character modules are augmentation kernels; all finite-level transition maps are surjective.

api.name: Kaletha16.D01.transport
api.statement: For E⊆K and n|m use norm K/E followed by the m/n power.

uses.how: Universal central coefficient group for rigidification.

items.name: Finite-level homomorphism identification
items.statement: If finite multiplicative Z/F is split by E and killed by n, evaluation at the distinguished coordinate identifies Hom_Gamma(u_(E/F,n),Z) with the norm-zero subgroup of Hom(mu_n,Z).

items.name: Vanishing of H1(F,u)
items.statement: For F=R or finite over Qp, continuous H1(Gamma,u)=0.

items.name: Second cohomology of u
items.statement: For F finite over Qp, continuous H2(Gamma,u) is canonically Zhat with the local-invariant normalization of§3.1.

items.name: Canonical gerbe class
items.statement: Under T03 choose xi corresponding to -1, and represent it by a continuous normalized two-cocycle with values in u. The sign is part of the normalization.

api.name: Kaletha16.D02.construct
api.statement: Choose the class corresponding to negative one.

api.name: Kaletha16.D02.characterise
api.statement: Changing its cocycle representative preserves the class.

api.name: Kaletha16.D02.transport
api.statement: Push xi forward by algebraic Gamma-equivariant maps u->Z.

uses.how: Fixes the enlarged Tate–Nakayama and transfer-factor signs.

items.name: Universal finite central obstruction class
items.statement: For every finite multiplicative Z/F, xi_*:Hom_Gamma(u,Z)->H2(Gamma,Z) is surjective.

items.name: Rigid Galois extension W
items.statement: Realize xi by a profinite extension 1->u->W->Gamma->1; in cocycle coordinates multiplication is (x,sigma)(y,tau)=(x sigma(y) xi(sigma,tau),sigma tau). W is distinct from the local Weil group W_F.
items.note: Use the existing FactorSet.Extension algebraic carrier L31 and add only P24 topology. P25 supplies the precise profinite classification; a continuous section is already built in L29.

api.name: Kaletha16.D03.construct
api.statement: Build the topological extension from the continuous cocycle.

api.name: Kaletha16.D03.characterise
api.statement: Recover its kernel, quotient and extension class.

api.name: Kaletha16.D03.transport
api.statement: A coboundary change of xi induces an extension isomorphism.

uses.how: Domain for the rigid cocycles.

items.name: Extension automorphisms are inner by u
items.statement: Every automorphism of W inducing identity on u and Gamma is conjugation by an element of u; extension realizations of xi are isomorphic, but not canonically so on raw cocycles.

items.name: Central-pair categories
items.statement: A consists of finite central multiplicative Z in an affine F-group G, with commuting-square homomorphisms. R is its full reductive connected subcategory and T its full torus subcategory.

api.name: Kaletha16.D04.construct
api.statement: Construct an object from a central closed immersion and affine group.

api.name: Kaletha16.D04.characterise
api.statement: Recognize the reductive and torus full subcategories by their group hypotheses.

api.name: Kaletha16.D04.transport
api.statement: Compose the commuting-square homomorphisms and preserve the central restriction.

uses.how: Functorial domain; Theorem4.11 is on R, not arbitrary disconnected A.

items.name: Rigid continuous cocycles
items.statement: For [Z->G] in A, Z1(u->W,Z->G) consists of continuous W-cocycles valued in discrete G(Fbar), whose restriction to u is an algebraic homomorphism into Z. The W-action factors through Gamma.

api.name: Kaletha16.D05.construct
api.statement: Build a rigid cocycle from its cocycle identity and algebraic central restriction.

api.name: Kaletha16.D05.characterise
api.statement: Read the algebraic map u->Z and ordinary quotient cocycle in G/Z.

api.name: Kaletha16.D05.transport
api.statement: Push cocycles along a morphism of central pairs.

uses.how: Carries extra normalization data of an inner twist.

items.name: Barred rigid cocycles and rigid H1
items.statement: Quotient D05 first by B1(W,Z) to obtain barred Z1, or by G(Fbar)-coboundaries to obtain the pointed set H1(u->W,Z->G). Only for commutative G is the latter naturally an abelian group.

api.name: Kaletha16.D06.construct
api.statement: Form the central-coboundary quotient and the full conjugacy quotient separately.

api.name: Kaletha16.D06.characterise
api.statement: Two H1 representatives agree precisely by a G-valued coboundary.

api.name: Kaletha16.D06.transport
api.statement: Extension isomorphisms give canonical barred Z1 and H1 identifications by T05.

uses.how: Use barred cocycles for canonical localization and H1 for isomorphism classes.

items.name: Inflation and restriction exactness
items.statement: Inflation H1(Gamma,G)->H1(u->W,Z->G) is injective and its image is the fiber of the trivial algebraic restriction in Hom_Gamma(u,Z). These are pointed sets for nonabelian G.

items.name: Abelian transgression sign
items.statement: For commutative G in A, the connecting map Hom_Gamma(u,Z)->H2(Gamma,G) is xi_* followed by Z->G with the negative-transgression convention, giving the exact sequence displayed in§3.3.

items.name: Finiteness of rigid H1
items.statement: For every [Z->G] in A over R or finite over Qp, H1(u->W,Z->G) is finite.

items.name: Split torus vanishing
items.statement: If S/F is a split torus and Z is finite central, H1(u->W,Z->S)=0.

items.name: Lifting all ordinary quotient cocycles
items.statement: For every affine G and finite central multiplicative Z, the map H1(u->W,Z->G)->H1(Gamma,G/Z) is surjective, including disconnected G.

items.name: Central-cohomology exact diagram
items.statement: For a central pair in A, the inflation/quotient maps fit the pointed exact rows of Proposition3.6; kernels and boundary maps agree with the ordinary central-extension sequence, and the right quotient map is T10.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

items.name: Anisotropic and fundamental torus reductions
items.statement: If reductive G possesses an anisotropic maximal torus, restriction H1rig(Z->G)->Hom_Gamma(u,Z) is surjective.

items.name: Every reductive inner form rigidifies
items.statement: For connected reductive G, taking Z=Z(Gder), the maps H1rig(Z->G)->H1(Gamma,G/Z)->H1(Gamma,Gad) are surjective. Thus every inner twist admits rigidification with finite Z.

items.name: Split-group fiber qualifications
items.statement: If G is split over a p-adic F and Z=Z(Gder), both maps H1rig(Z->G)->H1(F,G/Z)->H1(F,Gad) are bijections.

items.name: Abelianized rigid cohomology
items.statement: For [Z->G] in R, identify rigid cocycles z1,z2 when their relative ordinary cocycle in the inner twist G1 comes from H1(Gamma,G1sc); the quotient is H1_ab(u->W,Z->G). The simply connected group is twisted with z1.

api.name: Kaletha16.D07.construct
api.statement: Form the equivalence relation using the twisted simply connected cover.

api.name: Kaletha16.D07.characterise
api.statement: Test equivalence by a relative ordinary cocycle lifting to G1sc.

api.name: Kaletha16.D07.transport
api.statement: Push classes along reductive-group homomorphisms.

uses.how: Correct domain of the finite abelian duality.

items.name: When rigid H1 equals its abelianization
items.statement: If H1(F,Gprime_sc)=1 for every inner twist appearing in the rigid fibers, H1rig->H1ab is bijective. In particular this holds for p-adic F and for tori. Vanishing only for the untwisted Gsc is insufficient over R.

items.name: Torus quotient lattices and finite duality
items.statement: For Z->S in T, let Y=X_*(S)⊂Ybar=X_*(S/Z), Xbar=X^*(S/Z)⊂X=X^*(S). The quotient pairing (Ybar/Y)×(X/Xbar)->Q/Z is perfect.

api.name: Kaletha16.D10.construct
api.statement: Construct the inclusions and finite quotient pairing.

api.name: Kaletha16.D10.characterise
api.statement: Evaluate the pairing by lifting a rational cocharacter and reducing its character value modulo Z.

api.name: Kaletha16.D10.transport
api.statement: Dualize a morphism of central torus pairs contravariantly in characters.

uses.how: Lattice description of rigid classes and dual components.

items.name: Enlarged coinvariant torsion for tori
items.statement: For a finite Galois splitting field E/F, let I be its augmentation ideal and N its norm. Set Ybar_plus=Ybar/IY and take its torsion subgroup; the denominator is IY, not IYbar.

api.name: Kaletha16.D11.construct
api.statement: Form Ybar/IY and its torsion subgroup.

api.name: Kaletha16.D11.characterise
api.statement: Identify its torsion with ker(N:Ybar->Ybar)/IY.

api.name: Kaletha16.D11.transport
api.statement: Enlarging the splitting field gives the canonical same torsion object.

uses.how: The source of the enlarged Tate–Nakayama map.

items.name: Lattice norm exact sequence
items.statement: For D10 over a splitting E, there is an exact sequence 0->(Y_Gamma)_tors->(Ybar/IY)_tors->(Ybar/Y)^N->Y^Gamma/N(Y), where the final arrow is the lifted norm class.

items.name: Finite central restriction from cocharacters
items.statement: If n kills Ybar/Y, send lambdabar mod Y to the morphism mu_n->Z induced by n*lambdabar. Via T01 a norm-zero quotient class defines a Gamma-equivariant u->Z map, independent of sufficiently large (E,n).

api.name: Kaletha16.D12.construct
api.statement: Construct the finite central map from n*lambdabar.

api.name: Kaletha16.D12.characterise
api.statement: Its restriction to mu_n lands in Z and only depends on lambdabar mod Y.

api.name: Kaletha16.D12.transport
api.statement: Compare the maps after increasing n and the splitting field.

uses.how: Connects the explicit cocycle to its algebraic central restriction.

items.name: Reductive enlarged lattice quotient
items.statement: For reductive [Z->G], choose a maximal torus S, divide Y and Ybar by the coroot lattice Qvee, and take the colimit over finite splitting E of (Ybar/Qvee)^N / I(Y/Qvee). Transport by P15 makes this independent of S.

api.name: Kaletha16.D13.construct
api.statement: Construct the norm-kernel quotient at each splitting field.

api.name: Kaletha16.D13.characterise
api.statement: Identify conjugate maximal-torus presentations through the coroot quotient.

api.name: Kaletha16.D13.transport
api.statement: Induce maps for reductive homomorphisms using their simply connected lifts.

uses.how: Choice-free finite abelian source for reductive rigid duality.

items.name: Unbalanced cochain product
items.statement: For a continuous surjection from a compact group Delta to a finite group Theta, a discrete continuous Delta-module A and a Theta-module B, contract a degree-i homogeneous cochain whose last jprime variables factor through Theta against a degree-minus-j Tate cochain of B. For i≥jprime≥j>0 the result has degree i-j and its last jprime-j variables factor through Theta. Finite Delta is included; define the boundary subspaces i=j and j=0 explicitly.

api.name: Kaletha16.D14.construct
api.statement: Construct the finite contraction sum with the reversed variable order and group actions in§4.3.

api.name: Kaletha16.D14.characterise
api.statement: For j=0 recover ordinary cup product; for j=1 expose the inhomogeneous formula used in§4.5.

api.name: Kaletha16.D14.transport
api.statement: Commute with coefficient maps and compatible finite-quotient inflation.

uses.how: Produces explicit xi, transition corrections and the Tate–Nakayama cocycle.

items.name: Unbalanced Leibniz identity
items.statement: On the admissible cochain degrees and factorization subspaces of D14, the differential of f unbalanced-cup g is df cup g plus (-1)^deg(f) f cup dg, with the source boundary conventions.

items.name: Unbalanced finite-level compatibility
items.statement: The unbalanced product commutes with the coefficient and quotient maps used in§4.4; its inhomogeneous j=1 formula is the sum of f(g1,...,a) tensor g1...a acting on the negative-degree cochain.

items.name: Compatible relative Weil sections
items.statement: For a cofinal tower E_k/F choose relative Weil sections and representatives of the field-tower cosets compatibly: choose lifts in the Weil group first, then project them to the required coset representatives. Let c_k be the resulting normalized fundamental two-cocycles.

api.name: Kaletha16.D15.construct
api.statement: Choose the Weil lifts before the coset representatives and sections.

api.name: Kaletha16.D15.characterise
api.statement: Compute each c_k as the section multiplication defect.

api.name: Kaletha16.D15.transport
api.statement: Compare adjacent c_k through the actual quotient map and transfer.

uses.how: Supplies the tower identities needed to construct a continuous xi.

items.name: Relative Weil section product identities
items.statement: For the corrected sections D15 and sigma,tau in Gal(E_(k+1)/F), c_k(pi(sigma),pi(tau))=product_(v in Gal(E_(k+1)/E_k)) c_(k+1)(v*sigma,zeta_k(pi(tau))).

items.name: Coherent roots and quotient-torus extensions
items.statement: Choose positive n_k with every integer eventually dividing n_k and compatible set-theoretic n_k-th root maps l_k on Fbar units. Extend delta_e:Gm->Res_(E_k/F)Gm/Gm and the transition p between these quotient tori, not just their finite u-subgroups.

api.name: Kaletha16.D16.construct
api.statement: Choose compatible root maps and construct the extended quotient-torus homomorphisms.

api.name: Kaletha16.D16.characterise
api.statement: The extensions restrict to the finite-level delta_e and p on torsion.

api.name: Kaletha16.D16.transport
api.statement: Check the norm/power compatibility across adjacent levels.

uses.how: Types the explicit cochain formulas.

items.name: Explicit fundamental cocycles and transitions
items.statement: Set xi_k=d(l_k c_k) unbalanced-cup delta_e and alpha_k=(l_k c_k cup delta_e)^(-1) p(l_(k+1)c_(k+1) cup delta_e), using D16 to type both factors. Form W_k from xi_k and its alpha_k-adjusted transition maps.

api.name: Kaletha16.D17.construct
api.statement: Construct xi_k, alpha_k and the adjusted homomorphism W_(k+1)->W_k.

api.name: Kaletha16.D17.characterise
api.statement: Verify alpha_k takes values in u_k and d alpha_k=p(xi_(k+1))/xi_k.

api.name: Kaletha16.D17.transport
api.statement: Compose transitions to form the inverse-limit extension W.

uses.how: Provides the concrete representative of the canonical gerbe.

items.name: Explicit cocycles represent negative one
items.statement: For D17, alpha_k takes values in u_k and d alpha_k=p(xi_(k+1))*xi_k^-1, so the adjusted W_k transitions are homomorphisms.

items.name: Functorial evaluation of xi
items.statement: For algebraic phi:u->Z factoring through level k, phi(xi)=d(l_k c_k) unbalanced-cup (phi composed with delta_e), with the finite coefficient maps of Fact4.6.

items.name: Explicit enlarged Tate–Nakayama cocycle
items.statement: For a norm-zero lambdabar in Ybar choose k splitting S and killing Ybar/Y. Define z_lambdabar,k(x,sigma)=phi_lambdabar,k(x)*(l_k c_k unbalanced-cup n_k*lambdabar)(sigma). Extend phi to Res_(E_k/F)Gm/Gm by the norm-zero product of conjugate cocharacters when comparing levels.

api.name: Kaletha16.D18.construct
api.statement: Construct the displayed W_k cocycle.

api.name: Kaletha16.D18.characterise
api.statement: Its u-restriction is D12 and its change under lambdabar+IY is a coboundary.

api.name: Kaletha16.D18.transport
api.statement: Compare adjacent levels using the extended cocharacter map and alpha_k.

uses.how: Explicit map from the lattice torsion group to rigid H1.

items.name: Cocycle and level independence
items.statement: The cochain D18 is a continuous rigid cocycle and defines a class independent of all sufficiently large k, using the compatible roots, sections and transition maps.

items.name: Torus enlarged Tate–Nakayama isomorphism
items.statement: For [Z->S] in T over R or finite over Qp, D18 induces a natural isomorphism (Ybar/IY)_tors -> H1(u->W,Z->S), compatible with ordinary Tate–Nakayama at Z=1 and restriction to Hom_Gamma(u,Z).

items.name: Uniqueness of enlarged Tate–Nakayama
items.statement: There is at most one natural isomorphism from D13 to H1ab on R satisfying ordinary Tate–Nakayama compatibility and the central restriction square specified in§4.2.

items.name: Maximal-torus fibers of abelianized rigid cohomology
items.statement: For every maximal torus S in reductive [Z->G], each nonempty fiber of Ybar_plus,tor(Z->S) -> H1rig(Z->S) -> H1_ab(Z->G) is a torsor under the image of (X_*(Ssc)_Gamma)_tors in Ybar_plus,tor(Z->S).

items.name: Conjugacy independence of reductive classes
items.statement: Cocharacters in two maximal tori identified by geometric conjugation determine the same class in H1ab through the construction D18.

items.name: Reductive enlarged Tate–Nakayama duality
items.statement: For every [Z->G] in R, D13 is naturally isomorphic to H1_ab(u->W,Z->G), compatible with T27 on tori and with ordinary abelianized Tate–Nakayama at Z=1.

items.name: Rigid inner twists
items.statement: For connected reductive G/F and finite central Z, a rigid inner twist is (Gprime,psi,z) with psi an inner twist and z in D05 lifting psi^-1 sigma(psi) in Gad.

api.name: Kaletha16.D20.construct
api.statement: Construct a rigidification from a cocycle lifting the adjoint inner cocycle.

api.name: Kaletha16.D20.characterise
api.statement: Read the underlying inner form and its central restriction.

api.name: Kaletha16.D20.transport
api.statement: Enlarge Z by pushing the same cocycle through the central inclusion.

uses.how: Fixes transfer-factor and packet normalization.

items.name: Rigid inner-twist groupoid
items.statement: A morphism (G1,psi1,z1)->(G2,psi2,z2) is (f,g) with f:G1->G2 over F, z2(w)=g z1(w) w(g)^-1 and f psi1=psi2 Ad(g). Compose with the corresponding group elements; all morphisms are invertible.

api.name: Kaletha16.D21.construct
api.statement: Construct and compose a morphism from both compatibility equations.

api.name: Kaletha16.D21.characterise
api.statement: Isomorphism classes identify with H1rig(Z->G).

api.name: Kaletha16.D21.transport
api.statement: A morphism transports Gprime(F)-representations by f.

uses.how: Makes the compound packet independent of representatives.

items.name: Finite fixed-Z classes and enlargement
items.statement: For fixed finite central Z, the rigid inner-twist groupoid has finitely many isomorphism classes.

items.name: All rigid twists and K-groups
items.statement: Take the filtered union of D21 over finite central Z. Fibers of H1rig->H1ab define the K-groups used here. The all-Z set may be infinite; it need not be infinite, and is not generally functorial under arbitrary reductive homomorphisms.

api.name: Kaletha16.D22.construct
api.statement: Form the central-enlargement colimit groupoid.

api.name: Kaletha16.D22.characterise
api.statement: Recognize K-group membership by equality in H1ab.

api.name: Kaletha16.D22.transport
api.statement: Compare fixed-Z inclusions without asserting arbitrary-G functoriality.

uses.how: Domain for strong real forms and the relevance condition.

items.name: Rigid stable-conjugacy invariant
items.statement: For strongly regular delta in G(F), a rigid twist (psi,z), and delta_prime=psi(g delta g^-1) in Gprime(F), inv(delta,delta_prime) is the class of g^-1 z(w) w(g) in H1rig(Z->S), S=Cent_G(delta).

api.name: Kaletha16.D23.construct
api.statement: Construct the S-valued cocycle and its algebraic central restriction.

api.name: Kaletha16.D23.characterise
api.statement: Changing g by S or conjugating delta_prime rationally preserves its class.

api.name: Kaletha16.D23.transport
api.statement: Transport along a rigid groupoid morphism and the canonical stable centralizer identification.

uses.how: Pairs stable-conjugacy data with a refined dual element.

items.name: Stable classes across rigid forms
items.statement: The category of strongly regular representatives stably conjugate to fixed delta across rigid twists, with the morphisms of§5.1, has isomorphism classes H1rig(Z->S). On a fixed rigid twist the rational classes correspond to the fiber of H1rig(S)->H1rig(G) over [z].

items.name: Invariant of admissible torus embeddings
items.statement: For eta:S->G and eta_prime=psi Ad(g) eta, transport g^-1 z(w) w(g) back through eta^-1 to obtain the S-valued embedding invariant. Retain rationality and the admissible geometric conjugacy class.

api.name: Kaletha16.D24.construct
api.statement: Construct the invariant with the explicit eta^-1 transport.

api.name: Kaletha16.D24.characterise
api.statement: It is unchanged by the specified rational conjugacy of embeddings.

api.name: Kaletha16.D24.transport
api.statement: Compare embeddings in successive rigid twists using cocycle multiplication and transport.

uses.how: Labels real representations by torus rigid cohomology.

items.name: Representations of rigid inner twists
items.statement: A representation datum is (Gprime,psi,z,pi), with pi irreducible admissible and, for R, taken up to infinitesimal equivalence as in§5.1. Isomorphisms use D21 and representation transport.

api.name: Kaletha16.D25.construct
api.statement: Attach a representation to a rigid twist.

api.name: Kaletha16.D25.characterise
api.statement: Identify representation data under the rigid groupoid equivalence.

api.name: Kaletha16.D25.transport
api.statement: Transport characters using the induced F-isomorphism.

uses.how: Constituents of compound packets.

items.name: Strong real forms
items.statement: For real G with chosen conjugation sigma, a strong real form is delta in G(C) semidirect Gamma above sigma with delta squared central of finite order. Its real group is the fixed group of Ad(delta); morphisms are G(C)-conjugations.

api.name: Kaletha16.D26.construct
api.statement: Construct delta and its real fixed group from the finite-order square condition.

api.name: Kaletha16.D26.characterise
api.statement: Conjugate elements define isomorphic strong forms with the specified morphism.

api.name: Kaletha16.D26.transport
api.statement: Map a rigid cocycle to z(1,sigma)*sigma in compatible real gerbe coordinates.

uses.how: Comparison with the Adams–Barbasch–Vogan strong-form carrier.

items.name: Strong real forms equal all rigid real twists
items.statement: Over R the groupoid of all rigid inner twists, allowing every finite central Z, is equivalent to the strong-real-form groupoid D26.

items.name: Plus dual central subgroup
items.statement: For Gbar=G/Z define Z(Gbar_hat)^+ as the inverse image of Z(G_hat)^Gamma under the dual cover, and take its finite component group. Likewise for a torus use Sbar_hat^+.

api.name: Kaletha16.D27.construct
api.statement: Form the inverse image algebraic subgroup and its component group.

api.name: Kaletha16.D27.characterise
api.statement: Identify the exact central-cover maps and their connected kernels.

api.name: Kaletha16.D27.transport
api.statement: Transport along Z-enlargement by the induced dual maps.

uses.how: Dual target for abelianized rigid cohomology.

items.name: Lattice map to dual component characters
items.statement: There is a natural injection D13 -> Hom(pi0 Z(Gbar_hat)^+,Q/Z). It is an isomorphism for p-adic F or for tori; for real reductive G its image is the annihilator of the indicated norm subgroup N_(C/R)Z(Gbar_hat).

items.name: Abelianized rigid dual pairing
items.statement: There is a natural pairing H1_ab(u->W,Z->G) × pi0 Z(Gbar_hat)^+ -> Q/Z with trivial left kernel. It is perfect for p-adic F and for tori. Pullback to full rigid H1 is constant on K-groups and need not separate real rigid classes.

items.name: Ordinary endoscopy and z-pairs
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero local reductive G, use ordinary endoscopic data (H,Hext,s,eta), admissible matching of strongly regular classes, and z-pairs (Hz,eta_z) with induced central torus kernel and the required L-embedding.

api.name: Kaletha16.D30.construct
api.statement: Construct an ordinary datum and a compatible z-pair.

api.name: Kaletha16.D30.characterise
api.statement: Test ordinary datum equivalence and the domain of rational matching.

api.name: Kaletha16.D30.transport
api.statement: Transport data through dual isomorphisms, Levi embeddings and central extensions.

uses.how: Underlying data for refinement and the transfer factors.

items.name: Refined endoscopic data
items.statement: Relative to finite central Z, refine D30 by a lift dot_s in Z(Hbar_hat)^+ above s. An isomorphism must identify the lifted element in the specified component group, retaining the extra central information discarded by ordinary equivalence.

api.name: Kaletha16.D31.construct
api.statement: Choose the lifted central element and its ordinary image.

api.name: Kaletha16.D31.characterise
api.statement: Test refined isomorphism by equality in pi0 Z(Hbar_hat)^+.

api.name: Kaletha16.D31.transport
api.statement: Forget the lift to ordinary endoscopy or lift further after enlarging Z.

uses.how: Argument of the rigid dual character.

items.name: Finite refinements and enlargement compatibility
items.statement: Over fixed ordinary endoscopic data there are finitely many isomorphism classes of refinements for fixed Z. Enlargement of Z and a compatible lifted refined datum preserve the cohomological character factor.

items.name: Transfer factors with explicit convention
items.statement: Construct the relative factors and absolute normalizations using a-data, chi-data, splittings or Whittaker data, including the four LS/KS convention variants. A ratio identity alone fixes an absolute factor only up to C units; phase-only ambiguity requires a separately fixed modulus.

api.name: Kaletha16.D32.construct
api.statement: Construct each named factor from its auxiliary data and normalization.

api.name: Kaletha16.D32.characterise
api.statement: Recover the relative factor as the ratio of two absolute values on related regular pairs.

api.name: Kaletha16.D32.transport
api.statement: Transport auxiliary data and reciprocity conventions with the stated correction factors.

uses.how: Ordinary normalized supplier to the rigid correction.

items.name: Rigid normalized absolute transfer factor
items.statement: For a rigid twist (psi,z), refined datum dot_e, z-pair, and related strongly regular gamma_z,delta_prime, choose a stably related delta in the quasi-split G. Define Delta_rig=Delta_base(gamma_z,delta)*exp(2pi i pairing(inv(delta,delta_prime),dot_s))^-1.

api.name: Kaletha16.D33.construct
api.statement: Construct the factor using a matching quasi-split representative.

api.name: Kaletha16.D33.characterise
api.statement: Separate the base absolute normalization from the inverse rigid character factor.

api.name: Kaletha16.D33.transport
api.statement: Transport the base normalization coherently under an isomorphism of endoscopic data.

uses.how: Fixes the missing normalization on non-quasi-split groups.

items.name: Independence of the matching quasi-split representative
items.statement: The factor D33 is independent of the chosen stably related delta and satisfies the relative transfer-factor identity for Gprime.

items.name: Rigid and refined isomorphism invariance
items.statement: The factor D33 is invariant under isomorphisms of rigid twists and refined endoscopic data when the base absolute normalization is transported with those data, and compatible with the central enlargement in T50.

items.name: Relative-transfer comparison tori
items.statement: For matching pairs with centralizers S1,S2, use U=(S1sc×S2sc)/anti Z(Gsc) and V=(S1×S2)/anti Z(G), their central-pair variants and the dual comparison maps. The two section defects coincide, producing the relative U-cocycle.

api.name: Kaletha16.D34.construct
api.statement: Construct U,V and the central quotient maps with antidiagonal embeddings.

api.name: Kaletha16.D34.characterise
api.statement: The product of the two relative cochains descends to a cocycle because their differentials agree.

api.name: Kaletha16.D34.transport
api.statement: Compare the dual lifted elements and the rigid/ordinary Tate–Nakayama evaluations through U and V.

uses.how: Common comparison diagram for geometric and spectral transfer.

items.name: Tempered parameters and lifted centralizers
items.statement: For quasi-split G and tempered phi:W_Fprime->L G, with the real Weil group for R and the Weil–Deligne SL2 factor in the p-adic case, set S_phi=Cent_Ghat(phi) and S_phi^+ its inverse image under Gbar_hat->Ghat. Retain continuity, semisimplicity, bounded Weil image and algebraicity of the SL2 factor.

api.name: Kaletha16.D35.construct
api.statement: Form the parameter and its centralizers.

api.name: Kaletha16.D35.characterise
api.statement: Compute the finite component group pi0 S_phi^+ and its central restriction from pi0 Z(Gbar_hat)^+.

api.name: Kaletha16.D35.transport
api.statement: Transport parameters and centralizers under conjugation and Z-enlargement.

uses.how: Finite group governing the conjectural compound packet.

items.name: Refined local Langlands conjecture
items.statement: Conjectural specification: for each tempered phi, a Whittaker-normalized bijection from the compound packet of D25 across all Z-rigid twists to Irr(pi0 S_phi^+) commutes with the central-character map determined by T44; the trivial character labels the unique generic member on the quasi-split form. This is not asserted proved for general p-adic G.

api.name: Kaletha16.C01.construct
api.statement: State the conjecture as a proposition with the packet, central-character square and Whittaker normalization explicit.

api.name: Kaletha16.C01.characterise
api.statement: Specialize its fiber over a rigid inner twist and its relevance condition.

api.name: Kaletha16.C01.transport
api.statement: Formulate compatibility under increasing Z.

uses.how: States the unproved local input separately from the proved real case.

items.name: Stable and endoscopic packet distributions
items.statement: Conditional on C01, for a fixed rigid twist form the stable candidate e(Gprime) sum_pi dim(rho_pi) Theta_pi and, for dot_s, the weighted distribution e(Gprime) sum_pi tr(rho_pi(dot_s)) Theta_pi. The stability and matching-function character identity are separately conjectured in general.

api.name: Kaletha16.C02.construct
api.statement: Construct the finite dimension-weighted and trace-weighted sums.

api.name: Kaletha16.C02.characterise
api.statement: State stability and endoscopic transfer as propositions, with the matching-function domain.

api.name: Kaletha16.C02.transport
api.statement: Transport the distributions across rigid-twist isomorphisms.

uses.how: Targets proved using Shelstad for R.

items.name: Prime-convention rigid transfer
items.statement: Define Delta_prime_rig=Delta_prime_base times exp(2pi i pairing(inv,dot_s)), with the positive character factor. Compare Delta_prime for e with Delta for the inverted datum e^-1 exactly as in§5.6.

api.name: Kaletha16.D36.construct
api.statement: Construct the positive-pairing prime normalization.

api.name: Kaletha16.D36.characterise
api.statement: Prove the inversion-of-endoscopic-element convention conversion.

api.name: Kaletha16.D36.transport
api.statement: Use the same Whittaker and z-pair data in geometric and spectral comparison.

uses.how: Normalization used in the character identity.

items.name: Quaternion component-group example
items.statement: For the p-adic SL2 parameter of§5.4 with projective centralizer V4, S_phi^+=Q8. Its irreducibles have dimensions1,1,1,1,2; four have positive central character and one negative central character. The example has four split SL2 members and one inner SL1(D) member, with the latter dimension weight2.

items.name: Relevance and central-character annihilator
items.statement: A character of pi0 Z(Gbar_hat)^+ trivial on the kernel of its map to pi0 S_phi^+ corresponds under T44 to a relevant K-group for phi; over R this is a K-group condition, not a claim that every rigid twist in it is individually relevant.

items.name: Real Weil group and real parameters
items.statement: The real Weil group is C units union j C units with j z j^-1=conjugate(z) and j squared=-1. A real L-parameter is a continuous admissible homomorphism into the L-group over W_R, with temperedness given by bounded dual-group image.

api.name: Kaletha16.R01.construct
api.statement: Construct W_R with its topology and multiplication.

api.name: Kaletha16.R01.characterise
api.statement: Recover the two cosets, conjugation action and square relation.

api.name: Kaletha16.R01.transport
api.statement: Transport a parameter by dual-group conjugation and restriction to C units.

uses.how: Common real parameter carrier; import ordinary archimedean reciprocity rather than constructing a second Artin map.

items.name: Discrete real parameter torus and weights
items.statement: For a discrete real parameter, choose a dual Borel pair normalized by phi(W_R), write its C-unit restriction using dominant regular mu and the lambda datum with the quotient ambiguity specified in§5.6, and give X its phi(j)-twisted Galois action. This defines the real torus S and the admissible geometric class of S-embeddings.

api.name: Kaletha16.R02.construct
api.statement: Construct the twisted character lattice and corresponding real torus.

api.name: Kaletha16.R02.characterise
api.statement: Identify the allowed lambda changes and the regular dominant mu condition.

api.name: Kaletha16.R02.transport
api.statement: Transport the admissible embedding class through an inner twist.

uses.how: Torus whose rigid cohomology labels discrete series.

items.name: Discrete series from admissible torus embeddings
items.statement: For a discrete real phi and an inner form relevant to it, rational conjugacy classes of admissible S-embeddings label its discrete-series packet by the Langlands–Shelstad character construction Theta(eta(mu),eta(lambda),eta(Psi)); across all rigid twists use the corresponding embedding data.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

items.name: Whittaker-normalized discrete member
items.statement: For quasi-split real G, a fixed Whittaker datum selects a unique generic member of the discrete packet, hence its embedding eta_w, with the normalization used in§5.6.

items.name: Discrete compound packet bijection
items.statement: For discrete real phi, pi maps to inv(eta_w,eta_pi) in H1rig(Z->S); through the perfect torus pairing this gives a Whittaker-normalized bijection with Irr(pi0 S_phi^+), commuting with central characters and Z-enlargement.

items.name: Minimal cuspidal Levi and R-group roots
items.statement: For tempered real phi choose its minimal cuspidal Levi M, where it is discrete. With a maximal torus T_phi in S_phi^0, split the relevant normalizer quotient as W(S_phi^0) semidirect R_phi. Define Delta_phi^vee by vanishing on mu and zero sum over its R_phi orbit, as in§5.6.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

api.name: Kaletha16.R06.construct
api.statement: Construct M, the centralizer Weyl quotient and R_phi.

api.name: Kaletha16.R06.characterise
api.statement: Select the coroots satisfying both displayed parameter conditions.

api.name: Kaletha16.R06.transport
api.statement: Transport this root subsystem under parameter conjugation.

uses.how: Identifies the roots that enlarge M to the limit-discrete Levi.

items.name: Orthogonal A1 root subsystem
items.statement: The roots selected in R06 form a root system of type A1^r; phi(j) fixes their roots and acts by -1 on the relevant root spaces.

items.name: Corrected Cayley transform
items.statement: Choose one positive root from every opposite pair in Delta_phi^vee. For compatible root vectors put s_alpha=exp(i pi (X_alpha+X_-alpha)/4) and s=product of those positive-root factors. With theta=Ad(phi(j)), use s_alpha theta(s_alpha)^-1=s_alpha^2 and its reflection image in the Weyl group.

api.name: Kaletha16.R08.construct
api.statement: Construct the individual Cayley factors and the positive-root product.

api.name: Kaletha16.R08.characterise
api.statement: Compute theta(s_alpha)=s_alpha^-1 and the twisted-conjugation Weyl reflection.

api.name: Kaletha16.R08.transport
api.statement: Changing compatible choices transports the resulting Levi and parameter through the prescribed conjugacy.

uses.how: Corrects the printed construction before it is used in the real proof.

items.name: Limit-discrete parameter and coherent continuation
items.statement: Conjugate phi by the corrected s to obtain phi1 in the enlarged Levi M1. Choose a sufficiently dominant regular shift nu and coherently continue the discrete character at mu+nu to mu; the output is zero or an irreducible limit of discrete series.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

api.name: Kaletha16.R09.construct
api.statement: Construct M1 and phi1 with their embedding into G.

api.name: Kaletha16.R09.characterise
api.statement: State coherent continuation with the chosen shift and its zero-or-irreducible alternative.

api.name: Kaletha16.R09.transport
api.statement: Transport the output under admissible torus embeddings and compatible positive systems.

uses.how: Produces the tempered packet by induction from M1.

items.name: Noncompact-root criterion
items.statement: The coherent continuation in R09 attached to eta is nonzero exactly when every root eta(Delta_phi) is noncompact imaginary.

items.name: Real tempered packet embedding classification
items.statement: For every tempered real phi, the admissible embedding classes satisfying the noncompact-root condition of R10 correspond bijectively to its packet on a fixed inner form; the construction includes an empty set for an irrelevant form.

items.name: Levi injectivity in rigid cohomology
items.statement: For the real Levi M1 used above, H1rig(Z->M1)->H1rig(Z->G) is injective in the comparison needed for the packet construction.

items.name: Parity description of the packet image
items.statement: The injection of the real compound packet into H1rig(Z->S), obtained via the regular M1 packet, has image the classes whose image x in the adjoint torus cocharacter coinvariants satisfies <x,alpha> even for every alpha in Delta_phi.

items.name: Root-sign component subgroup
items.statement: Map the reflection generators of Omega(Delta_phi) to the component classes alpha(-1) in pi0(Sbar_hat^+). Their image is the annihilator of the parity subgroup in R13 under the torus pairing.

api.name: Kaletha16.R14.construct
api.statement: Construct the root-sign homomorphism from the A1^r Weyl group.

api.name: Kaletha16.R14.characterise
api.statement: Identify its character annihilator with the even-pairing classes.

api.name: Kaletha16.R14.transport
api.statement: Transport the map through the Cayley identification and central covers.

uses.how: Quotient converting the torus labels into parameter-centralizer labels.

items.name: Exact real component-group sequence
items.statement: For phi1 and S as above, Omega(Delta_phi)->pi0(Sbar_hat^+)->pi0(S_phi1^+)->1 is exact. Consequently the real lifted component group here is abelian, without an assertion that it has exponent2.

items.name: Refined real tempered packet theorem
items.statement: For every real connected reductive G, fixed finite central Z and Whittaker datum on its quasi-split form, every tempered phi has the compound packet bijection of C01 with Irr(pi0 S_phi^+), including the central-character square, generic normalization and Z-functoriality.

items.name: Stable real packet character
items.statement: For every fixed rigid real inner twist, e(Gprime) times the sum of the characters in its tempered packet (the real component labels are one-dimensional) is stable.

items.name: Real spectral transfer factor
items.statement: For a refined real endoscopic datum, its z-pair parameter phi_z and a member pi of the Gprime packet, use Shelstad spectral transfer on related parameters and set it to zero outside its related domain. The geometric factor is D36.
items.note: The source endpoint is recorded, but original-source definitions or auxiliary hypotheses still need declaration-sized decomposition. This contract is not a closed blueprint.

api.name: Kaletha16.R18.construct
api.statement: Construct the related-parameter spectral factor with the geometric normalization specified.

api.name: Kaletha16.R18.characterise
api.statement: Compare it to the product of the compatible factor and geometric factor on regular parameters.

api.name: Kaletha16.R18.transport
api.statement: Extend from regular parameters by coherent continuation and the stated Levi descent.

uses.how: Bridge from geometric rigid normalization to packet character labels.

items.name: Spectral factor equals rigid packet character
items.statement: With D36 as geometric normalization, the real spectral factor is e(Gprime)*<dot_s,pi>, where the bracket is the character label from R16 evaluated at dot_s.

items.name: Real endoscopic character identities
items.statement: For every tempered real parameter and related refined endoscopic datum, matching test functions for Delta-prime_rig satisfy the endoscopic character identity (5.11), with the weights tr(rho_pi(dot_s)) and the Kottwitz sign specified in C02.

items.name: Global rigid gerbe and localization interface
items.statement: For a number field F and the place/lift choices dot_V of Kal15b, import its profinite multiplicative P_dotV, extension E_xi,dotV, algebraic central-pair cocycles and localization maps to the local rigid cocycles modulo central coboundaries. The detailed global carrier is an external supplier, not constructed by this overview.

items.name: Global rigid lift of an inner twist
items.statement: For quasi-split number-field G with Gder simply connected as assumed in§5.7, the adjoint cocycle of an inner twist psi lifts through the global gerbe to a cocycle with central pair Z(Gsc)->Gsc; its localizations rigidify each local twist.

items.name: Localized refined endoscopic lifts
items.statement: For the global endoscopic datum and z-pair of§5.7, choose s_sc lifting the adjoint dual element and central y_v so s_der*y_v is Gamma_v-invariant. Let dot_s_v=(s_sc,y_v) in the dual cover for the physical central subgroup Z(Gsc).

api.name: Kaletha16.G04.construct
api.statement: Construct each local refined datum from s_sc and y_v.

api.name: Kaletha16.G04.characterise
api.statement: Check that the local obstruction vanishes and dot_s_v belongs to the required plus subgroup.

api.name: Kaletha16.G04.transport
api.statement: Compare local choices of y_v and the global lift through central characters.

items.name: Adelic product of rigid transfer factors
items.statement: Under§5.7 assumptions, including the existence of one rational related strongly regular pair, the canonical adelic transfer factor equals the product of the local Whittaker-normalized rigid transfer factors formed from G03–G04. The normalized unramified local factors are1 almost everywhere. This is unconditional, via Kal15b Proposition4.1.

items.name: Conditional adelic packet and global label group
items.statement: Assume the local conjecture C01 and the conjectural global Langlands group used in§5.7. For a discrete generic global parameter phi, form its finite adjoint centralizer component group with locally trivial obstruction, and the restricted tensor-product packet whose local labels are trivial at almost every unramified place.

items.name: Conditional adelic character pairing
items.statement: Under G06, the product of the local packet character evaluations defines a finite-dimensional character of the global component group, independent of s_sc, the y_v and the global rigidifying cocycle choices in the stated sense.

items.name: Conjectural discrete multiplicity formula
items.statement: For the tempered discrete automorphic representation and global parameter setting of§5.7, Conjecture5.11 predicts its multiplicity as the sum over relevant global parameters of the invariant dimension of the G07 character, equivalently the average of that character over the finite global component group.

items.statement: Assuming the local refined packet conjecture, the spectral mediating factors in§5.7 are expressed by the local packet character evaluations with the global rigidifying data; this additional spectral conclusion is conditional even though G09 is unconditional.

items.name: Real distribution characters
items.statement: For a finite-length admissible representation of a real reductive group in the Harish–Chandra/globalization category, define its trace distribution on compactly supported smooth test functions with fixed Haar measure; prove conjugacy invariance and representability by the regular semisimple character function in the source setting.

items.name: Real second cohomology of u
items.statement: For F=R, continuous H2(Gamma,u) is canonically Z/2 with the real Tate-invariant normalization of§3.1.

items.name: Split finite central obstruction comparison
items.statement: If finite multiplicative Z/F is split (its character action is trivial), the map xi_*:Hom_Gamma(u,Z)->H2(Gamma,Z) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Fundamental torus rigid surjectivity
items.statement: If S is a fundamental maximal torus of reductive G, then H1rig(Z->S)->H1rig(Z->G) is surjective.

items.name: Split real rigid fibers
items.statement: If G is split over R and Z=Z(Gder), H1(F,G/Z)->H1(F,Gad) is bijective and H1rig(Z->G)->H1(F,G/Z) has trivial neutral kernel. Nonneutral fibers can contain more than one class.

items.name: Relative Weil second product identity
items.statement: For the same data, c_k(pi(sigma),pi(tau))=product_(v in Gal(E_(k+1)/E_k)) c_(k+1)(sigma,v*tau)*c_(k+1)(sigma,v)^-1.

items.name: Explicit canonical gerbe class
items.statement: The compatible classes of xi_k in lim H2(F,u_k) equal the canonical class xi=-1 under Theorem3.1.

items.name: Full faithfulness of central enlargement
items.statement: For Z1⊆Z2 finite central, enlargement RI_Z1(G)->RI_Z2(G) is fully faithful.

items.name: Irreducible induction of the limit-discrete representation
items.statement: When the R09 coherent continuation on the specific enlarged Levi M1prime is nonzero, its normalized parabolic induction to Gprime is irreducible and tempered. This is not a theorem for arbitrary tempered inducing representations.

items.name: Normalized continuous sections of profinite quotients
items.statement: For a profinite group E and a closed subgroup H, the quotient E→E/H has a continuous section s with s(H)=1. More generally E/K→E/H has a normalized continuous section for K≤H. The section is a map of spaces, not necessarily a group homomorphism.

items.name: Finite towers have Mittag–Leffler stable images
items.statement: A cofiltered set-valued diagram with an eventually finite image at every index is Mittag–Leffler. In particular a tower of finite sets is Mittag–Leffler. Restricting a Mittag–Leffler diagram to its eventual ranges makes the transitions surjective and preserves its compatible sections. This is a set-level result; it does not itself construct lim¹ of abelian groups.

items.name: Existing factor-set group extension
items.statement: For an abstract group G acting by automorphisms on a commutative multiplicative group A and a normalized factor set c:G×G→A, use TauCeti.FactorSet.Extension with multiplication (a,g)(b,h)=(a·g(b)·c(g,h),gh). Its existing groupExtension has kernel A and quotient G. No topology is supplied by this declaration.

api.name: Kaletha16.L31.construct
api.statement: Use the existing Extension and groupExtension of a normalized FactorSet; the inverse is (g⁻¹·(a·c(g,g⁻¹))⁻¹,g⁻¹).

api.name: Kaletha16.L31.recover
api.statement: The canonical section g↦(1,g) has factor set c, and conjugation on A is the given G-action.

api.name: Kaletha16.L31.rescale
api.statement: If c(g,h)b(gh)=c′(g,h)g(b(h))b(g), rescaleEquiv sends (a,g) to (a·b(g),g); the inverse divides by b(g).

uses.how: Adds the product topology to this existing carrier, rather than defining a second algebraic extension.

items.name: Continuous cochains lift through a discrete quotient
items.statement: For a surjection p:B→C of underlying types, topological B and discrete C, every continuous f:X→C has a continuous lift e:X→B with p∘e=f. A set-theoretic section of p is continuous because its domain C is discrete; no compactness, additive structure or equivariance of the lift is required.

items.name: Built degree-one inflation–restriction exactness
items.statement: For a topological group G, normal subgroup N and continuous topological additive G-module M, with the induced continuous G/N-action on M^N, inflation H1(G/N,M^N)→H1(G,M) is injective and its range is the kernel of restriction to H1(N,M). This is the explicit continuous carrier and does not require the full Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.

items.name: The shift-difference presentation of lim and lim¹
items.statement: For a countable inverse sequence of abelian groups B_n with f_n:B_(n+1)→B_n, define Δ:∏B_n→∏B_n by Δ(x)_n=x_n−f_n(x_(n+1)). Identify lim B_n with ker Δ and lim¹ B_n with coker Δ as ordinary abelian groups. Short exact sequences of towers give the natural six-term kernel/cokernel exact sequence. For this index category these agree with the zeroth and first derived limit functors, and higher derived limits vanish.
items.locator: NSW2.7.4 pp140–141; exact proof read, with ordinary-group Delta description below

api.name: Kaletha16.P19.construct
api.statement: Construct the additive Delta map, its kernel and ordinary cokernel on the existing product and quotient carriers.

api.name: Kaletha16.P19.naturality
api.statement: A morphism of towers commutes with Delta and induces compatible maps on lim and lim¹.

api.name: Kaletha16.P19.connecting
api.statement: For 0→A_n→B_n→C_n→0 construct the six-term sequence 0→lim A→lim B→lim C→lim¹ A→lim¹ B→lim¹ C→0.

uses.how: Makes the exact obstruction to commuting a limit explicit.
The cochain product sequence induces this kernel/cokernel comparison.

items.name: Mittag–Leffler kills the shift-difference cokernel
items.statement: For a countable Mittag–Leffler tower of abelian groups B_n, Delta from P19 is surjective, hence lim¹ B_n=0. If the tower is ML-zero, both lim and lim¹ vanish. Finite groups at every level suffice for Mittag–Leffler, without surjectivity of the original maps.

items.name: Milnor sequence for a surjective finite-coefficient tower
items.statement: Let G be profinite and A_n finite discrete abelian G-modules with continuous actions and surjective equivariant transitions. Give A=lim A_n its inverse-limit topology. For q≥1 there is a natural exact sequence 0→lim¹ H^(q−1)(G,A_n)→H^q_cts(G,A)→lim H^q(G,A_n)→0. In degree zero invariants commute with the limit. H_cts is ordinary cohomology of continuous cochains with the stated coefficient topology.
items.locator: NSW2.7.5 pp141–142; surjective case of its proof

items.name: Stable-image reduction for arbitrary finite coefficient towers
items.statement: The exact sequence in P21 holds for any countable tower of finite discrete continuous G-modules, with no surjectivity assumption on transitions. Consequently H^q_cts(G,lim A_n)→lim H^q(G,A_n) is an isomorphism whenever the tower H^(q−1)(G,A_n) is Mittag–Leffler, in particular whenever those groups are finite. For q=1 no extra finiteness assumption is needed.

items.name: Finite local H¹ for finite coefficients
items.statement: For F finite over Qp and a finite discrete abelian G_F-module M, H¹(G_F,M) is finite, including residue-characteristic-primary M. For F=R, finite coefficients have finite cohomology in every nonnegative degree because G_F=C2 is finite.
items.locator: NSW7.1.8(iii), pp376–377; degree-one proof without local reciprocity; Kaletha Theorem3.1

items.name: Profinite topology on the existing factor-set extension
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group and A a profinite abelian group with jointly continuous G-action. For a continuous normalized factor set c:G×G→A, put the product topology on the existing L31 extension E_c. This is a profinite topological group and 1→A→E_c→G→1 is a continuous extension with closed embedded kernel and the quotient topology. The canonical section is continuous.
items.locator: NSW2.7.7 p143 and1.2.4 pp18–20; continuity adaptation of the pinned factor-set carrier

api.name: Kaletha16.P24.topologize
api.statement: Equip L31 with the topology transported from A×G and prove profiniteness and continuous group operations.

api.name: Kaletha16.P24.extension
api.statement: The inclusion identifies A with the closed kernel, projection induces the topological quotient G, and g↦(0,g) is a continuous normalized section in additive notation.

api.name: Kaletha16.P24.rescale
api.statement: For c′=c−db and continuous b, upgrade the existing rescaleEquiv (a,g)↦(a+b(g),g) to a topological extension equivalence; zero c recovers the topological semidirect product.

uses.how: Provides the explicit continuous realization of a cohomology class.
Realizes the fixed rigid class xi on the shared generic extension carrier.

items.name: Continuous H² classifies profinite extensions
items.statement: For profinite G and profinite abelian A with prescribed continuous action, H²_cts(G,A) is naturally in pointed bijection with equivalence classes of profinite extensions 1→A→E→G→1 inducing that action. Equivalence means a continuous group isomorphism inducing identity on A and G. A class is zero exactly when the extension has a continuous group-theoretic splitting.
items.locator: NSW2.7.7 p143; full Schreier proof1.2.4 pp17–20

items.name: Extension automorphisms and continuous one-cocycles
items.statement: For E_c as in P24, continuous extension automorphisms inducing identity on A and G form a group naturally isomorphic to Z¹_cts(G,A). In additive coordinates b acts by (a,g)↦(a+b(g),g). Conjugation by a0∈A corresponds to b(g)=a0−g·a0. Thus the quotient by these inner automorphisms is H¹_cts(G,A); if H¹=0 every such automorphism is inner, and its conjugating a0 is determined modulo A^G.
items.locator: Kaletha §3.2 p573; direct calculation on the NSW Schreier model

items.name: Deep powers and finite power classes over p-adic fields
items.statement: Let K/Qp be finite, pi a uniformizer, v the normalized valuation and n≥1 an integer. Then 1+pi^(2v(n)+1)O_K is contained in (K×)^n. The n-th-power subgroup is open and K×/(K×)^n is finite, including p|n. Only finiteness and this sufficient depth are asserted, not the sharp power-class cardinality formula.
items.locator: LocalFieldsRamification Layer1 power subgroup/finite-index targets; elementary complete-DVR contraction proof supplied here

items.name: Automorphisms of rigid inner twists are inner
items.statement: Every automorphism of a rigid inner twist (ψ, z): G → G' is given by an inner automorphism by an element of G'(F).
